newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack oil resumes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside says Cossack oil resumes.

text.p: The Cossack Pioneer oil platform offshore Western Australia has resumed production after shutting down for about eight hours on Wednesday due to bad weather, a spokesman for operator Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Thursday.
"By 9:00 a.m. this morning (0100 GMT) production was well and truly up," the spokesman said.
Cossack Pioneer, which has been producing about 65,000 barrels a day, was shut-in about on Wednesday morning due to an approaching tropical low, the spokesman said.
The rig remained connected to its riser and preparations began to resume production about late Wednesday afternoon as the storm moved away from the facility, he said.

Cossack Pioneer is owned eqally by the North West Shelf partnership of Woodside, The Broken Hill Pty Co ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd -- a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp -- Chevron Corp, and Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
